title: Lesson 4A — Endpoint Security
objective: Study-guide review — Day 3 — Zero Trust, IAM, Endpoint, and Network Engineering: Lesson 4A — Endpoint Security.

blocks.text: EDR and Endpoint Protection

Endpoint Detection and Response collects endpoint telemetry, detects suspicious behavior, supports investigation, and can assist response. Endpoint protection tools may include anti-malware, host firewall, device control, exploit protection, and policy enforcement. Teach the distinction: prevention blocks known or policy-violating actions; EDR helps detect, investigate, and respond.
Source: CertMaster Study Lesson 4A; M04 slides "Endpoint Detection Response" and "Endpoint Protection Tools".
Endpoint Protection Tool Classes
Endpoint protection is a control family, not one product. For teaching, break it into what each tool observes or enforces.

rows: Detect/block known malicious files or behavior
Reduce data exfiltration or malware introduction

blocks.text: Exam trap: endpoint protection does not replace least privilege or patching. A protected endpoint with local admin everywhere and outdated software is still weak.
Source: CertMaster Study Lesson 4A; M04 slides "Endpoint Protection Tools".
Endpoint Privilege Management

Endpoint privilege management reduces the risk of local administrator misuse. Users and processes should not run with unnecessary privilege. Temporary elevation should be controlled, logged, and scoped.
SecurityX cue: if malware or a user abuses local admin rights, remove standing privilege and enforce controlled elevation.
Source: CertMaster Study Lesson 4A; M04 slide "Endpoint Privilege Management".
Attack Surface Monitoring and Reduction

Endpoint attack surface includes installed software, exposed services, weak configuration, vulnerable agents, unnecessary privileges, and unmanaged devices. Monitoring identifies drift; reduction removes unnecessary exposure.
Practical teaching list:

items: Monitor process, network, and file activity.

blocks.text: Source: CertMaster Study Lesson 4A; M04 slide "Attack Surface Monitoring and Reduction".
Endpoint Threat-Actor TTPs

The official endpoint lesson includes threat-actor tactics, techniques, and procedures. Teach TTPs as behavior patterns that endpoint tools should help reveal: suspicious process execution, credential access attempts, persistence mechanisms, unusual script use, lateral movement from an endpoint, or abnormal privilege use.
Endpoint TTP decision cues:

items: Suspicious process tree: use EDR investigation.
Credential access pattern: inspect identity logs and endpoint telemetry.
Persistence on a workstation: inspect scheduled tasks, services, startup items, and scripts.
Lateral movement from endpoint: correlate endpoint, network, and authentication evidence.

blocks.text: Source: CertMaster Study Lesson 4A; M04 slides "Threat-actor tactics, techniques, and procedures".

MDM and Specialized Systems

Mobile Device Management manages mobile enrollment, configuration, compliance, and remote actions. Specialized and embedded systems may be harder to patch, monitor, or replace. The official source calls out industry-specific challenges and characteristics of specialized/legacy systems.
Compensating controls for specialized systems:
Source: CertMaster Study Lesson 4A; M04 slides "MDM", "Specialized and Embedded Systems".
Mobile Device Management

MDM gives the organization a way to enroll, configure, monitor, and respond to mobile devices. It is especially relevant when mobile devices access corporate data, email, SaaS applications, or internal services.
Common MDM controls:

items: Separation of personal and corporate data where supported.

blocks.text: Decision cue: if the scenario involves mobile access to business data, the answer often combines MDM, conditional access, data protection, and user privacy considerations.
Source: CertMaster Study Lesson 4A; M04 slide "MDM".

cheatsheet: Anti-malware: Detect/block known malicious files or behavior
Host firewall: Control inbound/outbound host traffic
Device control: Restrict removable media or peripherals
Application control: Allow or deny executable software
EDR: Investigate behavior and support response
